settings.heading: Choose 230Ah for the load.
settings.body: Get 2,560W of continuous output from a 20.6kg battery. It is the stronger choice for higher inverter demand when your route already includes regular solar, alternator or shore-power charging.

settings.heading: Enough reserve without carrying capacity you will not use.
settings.body: If you replenish from driving, solar or shore power most days, 230Ah keeps 2,944Wh onboard while saving 5.4kg versus the same-size 314Ah model.

settings.heading: Run the higher-load part of RV life with more headroom.
settings.body: A 2,560W continuous-output ceiling gives a correctly sized inverter system more room for kitchen bursts, cooling and the background loads already running.
settings.image_alt: SuntNeew 230Ah LiFePO4 battery supporting higher-demand RV kitchen and comfort loads

settings.heading: 200A continuous discharge—not just a bigger Ah number.
settings.body: Choose 230Ah when the electrical design needs the stronger continuous-current rating. Size the inverter, conductors, fuse, disconnect and terminals to the complete system limit.

settings.eyebrow: LESS WEIGHT IN THE SAME BAY

settings.body: Both large-capacity models share the stated 522 × 268 × 222mm enclosure. Choose 230Ah when structure, payload and service handling matter more than the extra reserve.

settings.heading: Fridge, network, lights—and the appliance you switch on next.

settings.heading: Know when to use the load—and when to recharge.

settings.heading: The details you need are ready before you build.

settings.body: Series and parallel layouts give larger RV builds a path to more voltage, output or reserve when identical batteries, balanced wiring, fusing and disconnects are planned as one system.

settings.question: How much energy does the 230Ah battery store?
settings.answer: The rated energy is 2,944Wh, calculated from the documented 12.8V and 230Ah ratings. Usable energy depends on system settings, load and operating conditions.

settings.question: Can I run a 200A load continuously?
settings.answer: 200A is the documented maximum continuous-discharge rating. The inverter, conductors, fuses, terminals and temperature conditions must also support the planned load.

settings.question: What charger size should I use?
settings.answer: The manual lists 46A as the recommended charge current and 115A as the maximum continuous charge current, using a 14.4V +/- 0.2V CC/CV profile. Coordinate all charging sources within those limits.

settings.question: Should I choose the 230Ah or 314Ah battery?
settings.answer: Choose 230Ah when 2,944Wh covers your time between charges and you want 2,560W continuous output, 5.4kg less weight and the lower current single-unit price. Choose 314Ah when 2,010W covers the load and the priority is 1,075.2Wh more reserve in the same 522 × 268 × 222mm enclosure. Test your devices in the Power Planner.

settings.question: Where can I review the complete operating limits?
settings.answer: The current English product manual is available in Documents on this page. Review it together with the charger, inverter and RV manufacturer instructions before installation.

settings.question: What conditions apply to the 6,000-cycle reference?
settings.answer: The 230Ah cycle-life reference is at least 6,000 cycles at 70% state of health (SOH), from the approved product data. Actual cycle life varies with depth of discharge, charge and discharge rate, temperature and operating conditions.
